## Introduction

The `targets` package is a tool for developing reproducible research workflows in R. Details of the package motivation and tools are described in detail: https://books.ropensci.org/targets/ and https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/.

### Example Workflow

1. Create a new R project

1. Run the `levinmisc::populate_targets_proj()` function in the R console - this function is described below in detail, and will initialize your project with helpful files/folders to start building your `targets` pipeline.

1. Keep input data in `Data/` and write pipeline outputs to `Results/`. Both directories, the `targets` data store, and logs are excluded from git, and a pre-commit hook blocks commits that would add data or participant identifiers. If the project was not yet a git repository, run `git init` and then `git config core.hooksPath .githooks`; a fresh clone of the project needs the second command once.

1. Open the project directory itself in code-server (File > Open Folder) and trust the workspace when prompted, so the editor tasks in `.vscode/tasks.json` load.

1. Modify the `Pipelines.qmd` file to specify your analyses. The `targets` documentation can be useful for specifics.

1. Knit/Render `Pipelines.qmd` to convert your markdown document into a series of R scripts that will actually run your analyses.

1. Run the pipeline. The `Pull, render, and run pipeline` editor task pulls the latest code from GitHub, renders the pipeline file, and runs `targets::tar_make()` in its own terminal, leaving your R terminal free. When the run finishes or fails, it can send a Slack or ntfy notification (see below). The run happens inside the code-server job, so request a session long enough for the whole pipeline.

1. Modify `Results.qmd` to present the results of your analyses. Rendering this file allows you to mix text describing your analyses/methods and include citations alongside the actual results of your pipeline. The `targets::tar_read()` function should be used heavily to load pre-computed results from your pipeline.

## populate_targets_proj()

The `populate_targets_proj` function can be run within a new project folder to initialize the project with the files/folders necessary for deploying a `targets` pipeline on the LPC at Penn. This includes creating a `Pipelines.qmd` file containing boilerplate for running analyses, a `Results.qmd` file which can be used to visualize the results, editor tasks, a pipeline run script with notifications, and git safeguards against committing data or participant identifiers.

The `runtime` argument chooses the R installation the pipeline runs against. `"native"` (the default) loads the LPC's R module (`module load R/4.5`) and leaves the package library to `renv`. `"container"` instead runs the main `targets` process and every LSF worker inside the LPC's RStudio Singularity image, reading packages from a library built against that image's R, which is the right choice only for a project whose library was built against that image. Mixing the two fails at run time: a worker that loads a library built for a different R version reports errors such as `unused arguments (controller = ...)`, because the worker and the controller end up running different `crew` versions.

The `"container"` runtime is still supported but will lose support in a future release, because the lab no longer runs R through Singularity. New projects should use the default `"native"` runtime. The editor tasks always use the native R module, whichever runtime is chosen.

```{r function-populate_targets_proj}
#' Create a minimal targets template in the current project
#' 
#' @description
#' This function creates a minimal targets template in the current directory. This includes creating a `Pipelines.qmd` file containing boilerplate for running analyses, and a `Results.qmd` file which can be used to visualize the results. Parallelization of the pipeline is implemented using [targets::tar_make()] and `crew.cluster`, using pre-filled using parameters specific to the LPC system at Penn.
#'
#' Files are written to `path`, which defaults to the working directory. Passing it explicitly matters when the
#' project directory holds none of the markers a project search looks for (an `.Rproj` file, a `DESCRIPTION`,
#' a git repository, a `.vscode/` directory), because such a search otherwise walks up and writes into a parent
#' directory.
#'
#' The `runtime` argument selects the R installation the pipeline runs against, and is passed through to [use_crew_lsf()]. `"native"`, the default, loads the LPC's R module and leaves the package library to `renv`; `"container"` instead runs the main `targets` process and every worker inside the LPC's RStudio Singularity image.
#'
#' The `"container"` runtime still works but will lose support in a future release; new projects should use `"native"`.
#'
#' The function also creates a data directory and a results directory, so that every location holding data or data-derived output is known when the project starts. With `git_safeguards = TRUE` (the default), it keeps those locations out of git in two ways. It appends entries to `.gitignore` for the data and results directories, the log directory, the `targets` data store (`_targets/`), the scripts generated from the Target Markdown file, and common data file types. Rendered HTML reports are not ignored, so they can be committed once checked. It also writes a pre-commit hook to `.githooks/pre-commit` that refuses any commit staging a file from those directories, a file with a data file extension, a file larger than 5 MB (25 MB for HTML), or text shaped like a PMBB participant ID, including IDs inside SVG figures embedded in a self-contained report. The hook prints only masked identifiers. When `path` is the root of a git repository, the function points `core.hooksPath` at `.githooks` so the hook runs; otherwise it prints the command to run after `git init`. Because the hook lives in the repository, each new clone needs only that one command.
#'
#' The function writes `.vscode/tasks.json`, which defines editor tasks for pulling from GitHub, rendering the pipeline file, and running the pipeline, plus one task that runs all three in sequence. The run task calls `.run-pipeline.R`, which runs [targets::tar_make()] and sends an optional Slack or ntfy notification when the pipeline completes or fails. The notification holds only the status, elapsed time, target counts, and errored target names, never error text, and is configured per user in `~/.Renviron` (see the vignette). The tasks work in VS Code and code-server when the project directory is opened as the workspace and trusted; an existing `tasks.json` is left unchanged. A run started from a task stops if the code-server job ends.
#'
#' The function can be re-run on an existing project to add files introduced by newer versions of this package. Existing files are kept unless `overwrite = TRUE`, and when `title` is not given, an existing `*-Pipeline.qmd` file supplies it. The pre-commit hook is the exception: it is always updated to the current version, and a previous hook that differs is saved as `.githooks/pre-commit.bak`.
#'
#' The LSF submission scripts `submit-targets.sh` and `.make-targets.sh` are written only when `lsf_scripts = TRUE`, for users who start pipelines from a submission host rather than from code-server on a compute node.
#'
#' @param title (character) base name for project files (eg. "{title}-Pipeline.qmd" and "{title}-Results.qmd")
#' @param log_folder (character) directory for LSF logs
#' @param path (character) project directory the files are written to, defaulting to the working directory
#' @param runtime (character) R runtime the pipeline and its LSF workers use: `"native"` (the default) for the module-provided R, or `"container"` for the LPC RStudio Singularity image
#' @param overwrite (logical) replace existing project files (the pipeline and results `.qmd` files, `.run-pipeline.R`, `.vscode/tasks.json`, and the LSF scripts) with fresh templates. By default, existing files are kept and only missing files are added.
#' @param data_dir (character) directory for input data, created inside `path` and excluded from git
#' @param results_dir (character) directory for pipeline results, created inside `path` and excluded from git
#' @param git_safeguards (logical) add `.gitignore` entries and a pre-commit hook that keep data, results, and participant identifiers out of git
#' @param lsf_scripts (logical) also write `submit-targets.sh` and `.make-targets.sh` for submitting the main `targets` process as an LSF job. The log folder is created either way, since `crew` LSF workers write their logs there.
#'
#' @export
#' @concept targets

populate_targets_proj <- function(title,
                                  log_folder = "build_logs",
                                  path = ".",
                                  runtime = c("native", "container"),
                                  overwrite = FALSE,
                                  data_dir = "Data",
                                  results_dir = "Results",
                                  git_safeguards = TRUE,
                                  lsf_scripts = FALSE) {
  runtime <- rlang::arg_match(runtime)

  # usethis::use_template() writes relative to the active usethis project, not
  # to the working directory, and usethis locates that project by walking *up*
  # from the working directory until a directory looks like one (.Rproj,
  # DESCRIPTION, .git, .vscode/, _quarto.yml, renv.lock, .here). A project
  # carrying none of those markers therefore sends every template into
  # whichever ancestor happens to have one. Pinning the active project to
  # `path` keeps the files where the user is working; force = TRUE skips that
  # same marker check, and local_project() restores the previous project when
  # this function exits.
  path <- fs::path_norm(fs::path_abs(path))
  fs::dir_create(path)
  usethis::local_project(path, force = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

  # Default the title to the one an existing project already uses, so a re-run
  # updates that project instead of adding a second pair of .qmd files. The
  # glob has to be matched against the directory: file.exists() takes globs
  # literally and so never matches anything.
  if (missing(title)) {
    existing_pipelines <- fs::path_file(fs::dir_ls(path, glob = "*-Pipeline.qmd"))
    title <- if (length(existing_pipelines) == 1) {
      sub("-Pipeline\\.qmd$", "", existing_pipelines)
    } else {
      basename(path)
    }
  }

  # Create build_logs folder
  fs::dir_create(path, log_folder)
  cli::cli_alert_success("Build log folder ready at {.file {fs::path(path, log_folder)}}")

  # Create data and results folders, so every location that holds data or
  # data-derived output exists, and is excluded from git, from the start
  fs::dir_create(path, c(data_dir, results_dir))
  cli::cli_alert_success("Data folder ready at {.file {fs::path(path, data_dir)}}")
  cli::cli_alert_success("Results folder ready at {.file {fs::path(path, results_dir)}}")

  if (lsf_scripts) {
    # Copy batch script for job submission. The main {targets} process has to
    # run under the same R as the workers, so the runtime chooses the template.
    make_targets_template <- switch(runtime,
      container = ".make-targets.sh",
      native = ".make-targets-native.sh"
    )
    write_project_template(make_targets_template, ".make-targets.sh", path, overwrite,
                           data = function() list(r_module = lpc_r_module),
                           label = paste("Submission template for the", runtime, "R runtime"))

    # Copy batch script to submit targets job
    write_project_template("submit-targets.sh", "submit-targets.sh", path, overwrite,
                           label = "Targets submission script")
  }

  # Copy targets pipeline template. use_crew_lsf() prints its code block, so it
  # runs only when the file is actually written.
  write_project_template("Pipeline.qmd", paste0(title, "-Pipeline.qmd"), path, overwrite,
                         data = function() list(global_options = levinmisc::use_crew_lsf(runtime = runtime, path = path)),
                         label = "Targets Pipeline template")

  # Copy targets results template
  write_project_template("Results.qmd", paste0(title, "-Results.qmd"), path, overwrite,
                         label = "Targets Results template")

  # Script the run task calls: runs tar_make() and sends the notification
  write_project_template("run-pipeline.R", ".run-pipeline.R", path, overwrite,
                         label = "Pipeline run script")

  # Editor tasks for pulling, rendering, and running
  tasks_written <- write_project_template("tasks.json", ".vscode/tasks.json", path, overwrite,
                                          data = function() list(title = title, r_module = lpc_r_module),
                                          label = "Editor tasks")
  if (tasks_written) {
    cli::cli_alert_info("To use the editor tasks: open {.file {path}} itself as the code-server workspace, trust it when prompted, and optionally add the keybinding shown at the top of {.file .vscode/tasks.json} to your user {.file keybindings.json}.")
    if (runtime == "container") {
      cli::cli_alert_info("The editor tasks use the native R module ({.val {lpc_r_module}}), not the container.")
    }
  }

  if (git_safeguards) {
    use_targets_git_safeguards(path,
                               data_dir = data_dir,
                               results_dir = results_dir,
                               log_folder = log_folder)
  }

  invisible(path)
}

#' R module loaded by the native runtime, the editor tasks, and LSF workers
#' @noRd
lpc_r_module <- "R/4.5"

#' Write a template into the project unless the file already exists
#'
#' Existing files are kept unless `overwrite` is TRUE, so populate_targets_proj()
#' can be re-run to add files that newer package versions introduce. The file is
#' deleted before rewriting because usethis::use_template() would otherwise ask
#' again, or silently decline outside an interactive session.
#'
#' @param template,save_as (character) template name and path relative to `path`
#' @param path (character) project directory, already the active usethis project
#' @param overwrite (logical) replace an existing file
#' @param data (function) returns the template data; called only when writing
#' @param label (character) description used in the status message
#' @return TRUE if the file was written, FALSE if an existing file was kept
#' @noRd
write_project_template <- function(template, save_as, path, overwrite,
                                   data = function() list(), label = save_as) {
  target <- fs::path(path, save_as)
  if (fs::file_exists(target) && !overwrite) {
    cli::cli_alert_info("Kept existing {.file {save_as}}")
    return(invisible(FALSE))
  }
  if (fs::file_exists(target)) {
    fs::file_delete(target)
  }
  fs::dir_create(fs::path_dir(target))
  usethis::use_template(template, save_as = save_as, data = data(), package = "levinmisc")
  cli::cli_alert_success("{label} created at {.file {save_as}}")
  invisible(TRUE)
}

#' Add .gitignore entries and a pre-commit hook that keep data out of git
#'
#' @param path (character) normalized project directory, already set as the active usethis project
#' @param data_dir,results_dir,log_folder (character) directories to exclude
#'
#' @noRd
use_targets_git_safeguards <- function(path, data_dir, results_dir, log_folder) {
  dirs <- sub("/+$", "", c(data_dir, results_dir, log_folder))

  usethis::use_git_ignore(c(
    "# Data, results, and logs (levinmisc::populate_targets_proj)",
    paste0("/", dirs, "/"),
    "/_targets/",
    "# Scripts generated by rendering the Target Markdown pipeline file",
    "/_targets.R",
    "/_targets_r/",
    "# Supporting folders of non-self-contained reports",
    "*_files/",
    "/.quarto/",
    "# Common data and serialized-object file types",
    "*.rds", "*.rda", "*.RData", "*.qs", "*.qs2", "*.fst",
    "*.parquet", "*.feather", "*.arrow",
    "# Synthetic test fixtures may be committed",
    "!/tests/**",
    "!/Synthetic/**",
    "# R session files",
    ".Rhistory",
    ".Rproj.user/"
  ))
  cli::cli_alert_success("Data, results, and generated files added to {.file .gitignore}")

  # Projects created by earlier versions ignored all rendered HTML
  ignored <- trimws(readLines(fs::path(path, ".gitignore"), warn = FALSE))
  if (any(ignored %in% c("*.html", "/*.html", "*.htm"))) {
    cli::cli_alert_warning("{.file .gitignore} still ignores {.code *.html}, so rendered reports cannot be committed. Remove that line to commit reports; the pre-commit hook checks them for participant identifiers.")
  }

  # The hook matches paths with bash regular expressions, so directory names
  # containing regex metacharacters (eg. ".") have to be escaped
  regex_escape <- function(x) gsub("([.|()^{}+$*?\\[\\]\\\\])", "\\\\\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
  # The hook is always brought up to date, unlike other project files, so
  # older projects gain new checks. A previous version that differs, possibly
  # edited by hand, is kept beside it.
  hook <- fs::path(path, ".githooks", "pre-commit")
  previous_hook <- if (fs::file_exists(hook)) readLines(hook, warn = FALSE) else NULL
  if (!is.null(previous_hook)) {
    fs::file_delete(hook)
  }
  fs::dir_create(path, ".githooks")
  usethis::use_template("pre-commit",
                        save_as = ".githooks/pre-commit",
                        data = list(data_dir = regex_escape(dirs[[1]]),
                                    results_dir = regex_escape(dirs[[2]]),
                                    log_folder = regex_escape(dirs[[3]])),
                        package = "levinmisc")
  fs::file_chmod(hook, "u+x")
  if (is.null(previous_hook)) {
    cli::cli_alert_success("Pre-commit hook created at {.file .githooks/pre-commit}")
  } else if (identical(previous_hook, readLines(hook, warn = FALSE))) {
    cli::cli_alert_info("Pre-commit hook at {.file .githooks/pre-commit} is already up to date")
  } else {
    writeLines(previous_hook, fs::path(path, ".githooks", "pre-commit.bak"))
    cli::cli_alert_success("Pre-commit hook updated; the previous version is saved as {.file .githooks/pre-commit.bak}")
  }

  # Git runs hooks from core.hooksPath, resolved relative to the repository
  # root, so the setting only applies when `path` is that root. An existing
  # hooksPath belongs to another tool (eg. a pre-commit framework) and is kept.
  activate_cmd <- "git config core.hooksPath .githooks"
  git <- function(...) {
    tryCatch(
      processx::run("git", c("-C", path, ...), error_on_status = FALSE),
      error = function(e) list(status = 1L, stdout = "")
    )
  }
  # `--show-prefix` prints the path from the repository root to `path`, which
  # is empty at the root. Asking git avoids comparing path strings, which
  # differ on Windows (drive letters, short 8.3 names, slashes).
  prefix <- git("rev-parse", "--show-prefix")
  is_repo_root <- prefix$status == 0 && !nzchar(trimws(prefix$stdout))

  if (!is_repo_root) {
    cli::cli_alert_info("{.file {path}} is not the root of a git repository. After {.code git init}, activate the hook with {.code {activate_cmd}}")
    return(invisible(FALSE))
  }

  current <- trimws(git("config", "--get", "core.hooksPath")$stdout)
  if (nzchar(current) && current != ".githooks") {
    cli::cli_alert_warning("Kept existing {.code core.hooksPath = {current}}. Copy {.file .githooks/pre-commit} there to use the hook.")
    return(invisible(FALSE))
  }

  git("config", "core.hooksPath", ".githooks")
  cli::cli_alert_success("Pre-commit hook activated. Each new clone needs {.code {activate_cmd}} once.")
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

```{r examples-populate_targets_proj, eval=FALSE}
#' \dontrun{
populate_targets_proj("test")
```

The `populate_targets_proj()` function creates several files/folders within the project directory:

  - `Pipeline.qmd` - Quarto markdown file which can be used to create a Target Markdown document that specifies a `targets` pipeline for your analyses. See: https://books.ropensci.org/targets/literate-programming.html#target-markdown for details. Remember to knit/render this document in order to generate the pipeline.
  
  - `Results.qmd` - Quarto markdown file which can be used to display the results generated by the `targets` pipeline specified in `Pipeline.qmd`. It renders a self-contained HTML report, which can be committed once the pre-commit hook has checked it.
  
  - `build_logs/` - Directory where `crew` LSF worker logs are stored

  - `Data/` and `Results/` - Directories for input data and pipeline outputs; their names are set by the `data_dir` and `results_dir` arguments. Both are excluded from git.

  - `.run-pipeline.R` - Script the editor's run task calls. It runs `targets::tar_make()`, prints a summary, sends an optional notification, and exits with status 1 if the pipeline failed.

  - `.vscode/tasks.json` - Editor tasks to pull from GitHub, render the pipeline file, run the pipeline, or do all three in sequence (`Pull, render, and run pipeline`), plus a task to render the results report. Code-server loads the file only when the project directory itself is opened as the workspace and trusted. The comment at the top of the file shows the keybinding to add to your user `keybindings.json` to run the combined task with one key, and a second keybinding that sends `targets::tar_make()` to the active R terminal instead.

  - `.gitignore` - Entries added for the data, results, and log directories, the `targets` data store (`_targets/`), scripts generated by rendering the pipeline file, and common data file types. Rendered HTML reports are not ignored. Existing entries are kept.

  - `.githooks/pre-commit` - Git hook that blocks any commit staging a file from a protected directory, a file with a data file extension, a file larger than 5 MB (25 MB for HTML reports), or text shaped like a PMBB participant ID. Set `git_safeguards = FALSE` to skip both the `.gitignore` entries and the hook. Details are below.

### Participant identifier check

The pre-commit hook searches every staged text file for strings shaped like a PMBB ID: `PMBB` followed by digits, in upper or lower case, with an optional space, underscore, or dash. The pattern also matches truncated IDs and IDs inside longer strings, such as `sample_PMBB…_A`. It decodes SVG figures embedded in self-contained HTML reports and searches their text too; text drawn inside PNG figures cannot be checked. The hook uses ripgrep (`rg`) when it is installed and `grep` otherwise, with identical results, and needs no configuration or identifier list.

When it finds an identifier, the hook blocks the commit and lists each file and line with the value masked (for example `PM************`), so its output is safe to share. Fix the source of the report, for example by not printing an ID column, re-render, and stage the file again. To add other identifier shapes, extend `ID_PATTERN` in `.githooks/pre-commit` with regular-expression alternation (`'pattern1|pattern2'`). After checking a file yourself, `git commit --no-verify` bypasses the hook once.

### Pipeline notifications

`.run-pipeline.R` can notify you when a pipeline completes or fails. The message contains the status, elapsed time, target counts, and the names of errored targets. It never contains error messages or target values, because R errors can echo data values and the message leaves the cluster; the full error is printed in the task terminal. Notifications are sent with the `curl` command-line tool, so no extra R packages are needed in the project library. They are configured once per user in `~/.Renviron`, never in the project.

**Slack.** Create an incoming webhook for the channel that should receive messages:

1. Go to https://api.slack.com/apps, choose **Create New App**, then **From scratch**, and pick the lab workspace.
1. Open **Incoming Webhooks** and switch on the activation toggle.
1. Choose **Add New Webhook to Workspace**, pick the channel, and select **Authorize**. If the workspace restricts apps, this becomes a request that a workspace admin must approve.
1. Copy the webhook URL and add these lines to `~/.Renviron`, then restart R:

```
LEVINMISC_NOTIFY=slack
LEVINMISC_SLACK_WEBHOOK=https://hooks.slack.com/services/...
```

Treat the webhook URL like a password: anyone who has it can post to the channel. The Slack desktop and phone apps show each message as a notification.

**ntfy.** As an alternative, ntfy (https://ntfy.sh) delivers push notifications to its phone app, Mac app, or website. Subscribe to a hard-to-guess topic, then add:

```
LEVINMISC_NOTIFY=ntfy
LEVINMISC_NTFY_URL=https://ntfy.sh/your-hard-to-guess-topic
```

Set `LEVINMISC_NOTIFY_START=true` to also be notified when a run starts. With `LEVINMISC_NOTIFY` unset, the script prints its summary in the terminal only.

### Updating an existing project

Re-run `populate_targets_proj()` in an existing project to add files introduced by newer versions of this package, such as `.run-pipeline.R` or the editor tasks. Existing files, including your `Pipeline.qmd` and `Results.qmd`, are kept, and the function lists each one it kept. When `title` is not given and the project has one `*-Pipeline.qmd` file, its name supplies the title. Pass `overwrite = TRUE` only to replace existing files with fresh templates.

The pre-commit hook is the exception: a re-run always updates it, so older projects gain the identifier check, and a previous version that differs is saved as `.githooks/pre-commit.bak`. If the project's `.gitignore` still contains a `*.html` line from an earlier version, the function warns; delete that line to commit rendered reports. LSF scripts from earlier versions, such as `submit-targets.sh`, are left in place.

## Optional LSF submission scripts

Pipelines are normally run from code-server on a compute node with the editor task above. To submit the main `targets` process as its own LSF job instead, for example from a submission host such as `scisub7`, call `populate_targets_proj(lsf_scripts = TRUE)`. This also writes `submit-targets.sh` and the hidden helper `.make-targets.sh`, whose contents follow the `runtime` argument so that the main `targets` process runs under the same R as the workers. Run `submit-targets.sh` from the root directory of your project once `Pipeline.qmd` has been knit/rendered. The script accepts command line arguments:
  
```
Usage: ./submit-targets.sh [-n NUM_WORKERS] [-j JOB_NAME] [-o OUTPUT_LOG] [-e ERROR_LOG] [-q QUEUE] [-m MEMORY] [-s SLACK] [-h HELP]

Submit a job using the LSF scheduler with the specified number of CPUs and memory usage.

Options:
  -n NUM_WORKERS Number of workers (cpu cores) to request for running the targets pipeline (default: 1)
  -j JOB_NAME    Name of the job (default: make_targets)
  -o OUTPUT_LOG  Path to the output log file (default: build_logs/targets_%J.out)
  -e ERROR_LOG   Path to the error log file (default: build_logs/targets_%J.err)
  -q QUEUE       Name of the queue to submit the job to (default: voltron_normal)
  -m MEMORY      Memory usage for the job in megabytes (default: 16000)
  -s SLACK       Enable slack notifications; requires setup using slackr::slack_setup() (default: false)
  -h HELP        Display this help message and exit
```

The `-s true` flag of `submit-targets.sh` sends start and finish messages through the `slackr` package, which must be installed and configured separately (https://mrkaye97.github.io/slackr/index.html). It does not report failures; the webhook notifications from `.run-pipeline.R` described above do.

```{r tests-populate_targets_proj}
test_that("populate_targets_proj works", {
  expect_true(inherits(populate_targets_proj, "function"))
})

test_that("populate_targets_proj creates data folders and git safeguards", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_if(Sys.which("git") == "", "git is not installed")
  proj <- withr::local_tempdir()
  processx::run("git", c("-C", proj, "init", "-q"))

  suppressMessages(populate_targets_proj("test", path = proj, overwrite = TRUE))

  expect_true(dir.exists(file.path(proj, "Data")))
  expect_true(dir.exists(file.path(proj, "Results")))
  expect_true(file.exists(file.path(proj, ".vscode", "tasks.json")))

  ignore <- readLines(file.path(proj, ".gitignore"))
  expect_true(all(c("/Data/", "/Results/", "/_targets/") %in% ignore))

  hook <- file.path(proj, ".githooks", "pre-commit")
  expect_true(file.exists(hook))
  # Windows has no execute permission bit; git for Windows runs hooks regardless
  if (.Platform$OS.type != "windows") {
    expect_true(file.access(hook, mode = 1) == 0)
  }
  hooks_path <- processx::run("git", c("-C", proj, "config", "--get", "core.hooksPath"))$stdout
  expect_equal(trimws(hooks_path), ".githooks")
})

test_that("re-running populate_targets_proj keeps existing files and adds missing ones", {
  skip_on_cran()
  proj <- withr::local_tempdir()
  processx::run("git", c("-C", proj, "init", "-q"))
  writeLines("my pipeline", file.path(proj, "study-Pipeline.qmd"))
  writeLines("my results", file.path(proj, "study-Results.qmd"))
  writeLines(c(".Rhistory", "*.html"), file.path(proj, ".gitignore"))
  dir.create(file.path(proj, ".githooks"))
  writeLines("#!/bin/sh\necho old hook", file.path(proj, ".githooks", "pre-commit"))

  messages <- testthat::capture_messages(populate_targets_proj(path = proj))

  # Title comes from the existing file, so no second pair of .qmd files appears
  expect_equal(length(fs::dir_ls(proj, glob = "*-Pipeline.qmd")), 1)
  expect_equal(readLines(file.path(proj, "study-Pipeline.qmd")), "my pipeline")
  expect_equal(readLines(file.path(proj, "study-Results.qmd")), "my results")
  expect_true(any(grepl("Kept existing", messages)))
  expect_false(any(grepl("Targets Pipeline template created", messages)))

  # Missing files are added
  expect_true(file.exists(file.path(proj, ".run-pipeline.R")))
  tasks <- paste(readLines(file.path(proj, ".vscode", "tasks.json")), collapse = "\n")
  expect_true(grepl("study-Pipeline.qmd", tasks, fixed = TRUE))

  # The hook is updated and the old one kept; the *.html ignore line is reported
  expect_true(any(grepl("ID_PATTERN", readLines(file.path(proj, ".githooks", "pre-commit")))))
  expect_equal(readLines(file.path(proj, ".githooks", "pre-commit.bak"))[2], "echo old hook")
  expect_true(any(grepl("still ignores", messages)))

  # A second re-run reports the hook as current and writes no new backup
  file.remove(file.path(proj, ".githooks", "pre-commit.bak"))
  messages <- testthat::capture_messages(populate_targets_proj(path = proj))
  expect_true(any(grepl("already up to date", messages)))
  expect_false(file.exists(file.path(proj, ".githooks", "pre-commit.bak")))
})

test_that("populate_targets_proj replaces existing files when overwrite = TRUE", {
  skip_on_cran()
  proj <- withr::local_tempdir()
  writeLines("my pipeline", file.path(proj, "study-Pipeline.qmd"))
  suppressMessages(populate_targets_proj("study", path = proj, overwrite = TRUE, git_safeguards = FALSE))

})

  proj2 <- withr::local_tempdir()

})

test_that("populate_targets_proj writes native-R editor tasks and the run script", {
  skip_on_cran()
  proj <- withr::local_tempdir()
  suppressMessages(populate_targets_proj("test", path = proj, overwrite = TRUE, runtime = "container"))
  tasks <- paste(readLines(file.path(proj, ".vscode", "tasks.json")), collapse = "\n")
  expect_true(grepl(paste0("module load ", lpc_r_module, " && Rscript .run-pipeline.R"), tasks, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_true(grepl("quarto render \\\"test-Pipeline.qmd\\\"", tasks, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_false(grepl("singularity", tasks, fixed = TRUE))
  # A login shell would run the compute node's profile guard and stop the task
  expect_true(grepl('"args": ["-c"]', tasks, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_true(file.exists(file.path(proj, ".run-pipeline.R")))
  expect_false("*.html" %in% readLines(file.path(proj, ".gitignore")))
})

# Helpers for the pre-commit hook tests. `with_rg = FALSE` runs git with a PATH
# that lacks ripgrep, so the grep code path is exercised.
hook_project <- function() {
  proj <- withr::local_tempdir(.local_envir = parent.frame())
  processx::run("git", c("-C", proj, "init", "-q"))
  processx::run("git", c("-C", proj, "config", "user.email", "test@example.com"))
  processx::run("git", c("-C", proj, "config", "user.name", "Test"))
  suppressMessages(populate_targets_proj("test", path = proj, overwrite = TRUE))
  proj
}

path_without_rg <- function() {
  bin <- withr::local_tempdir(.local_envir = parent.frame())
  tools <- c("bash", "sh", "env", "git", "grep", "sed", "base64", "cut", "tr",
             "mktemp", "rm", "cat", "head", "printf")
  for (tool in tools) {
    location <- Sys.which(tool)
    if (nzchar(location)) file.symlink(location, file.path(bin, tool))
  }
  bin
}

try_commit <- function(proj, files, with_rg = TRUE) {
  for (name in names(files)) {
    dir.create(dirname(file.path(proj, name)), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    writeLines(files[[name]], file.path(proj, name))
  }
  processx::run("git", c("-C", proj, "add", "-f", names(files)))
  env <- if (with_rg) NULL else c(PATH = path_without_rg())
  git <- Sys.which("git")
  processx::run(git, c("-C", proj, "commit", "-q", "-m", "test"),
                env = if (is.null(env)) NULL else c("current", env),
                error_on_status = FALSE)
}

fake_id <- "PMBB0000000012345"
svg_uri <- function(text) {
  svg_file <- withr::local_tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
  writeLines(sprintf('<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><text>%s</text></svg>', text), svg_file)
  encoded <- processx::run("sh", c("-c", paste("base64 <", shQuote(svg_file))))$stdout
  paste0("data:image/svg+xml;base64,", gsub("\n", "", encoded))
}

hook_cases <- function() {
  png_noise <- paste(sample(c(LETTERS, letters, 0:9, "+", "/"), 2e5, replace = TRUE), collapse = "")
  genomics <- paste(sprintf("<tr><td>chr1:%d</td><td>rs%d</td></tr>",
                            sample.int(2.4e8, 2000), sample.int(9e8, 2000)), collapse = "")
  list(
    body_text   = list(files = list("report.html" = sprintf("<p>Participant %s</p>", fake_id)), blocked = TRUE),
    widget_json = list(files = list("report.html" = sprintf('<script type="application/json">{"x":{"data":[["%s"]]}}</script>', fake_id)), blocked = TRUE),
    svg_only    = list(files = list("report.html" = sprintf('<img src="%s">', svg_uri(fake_id))), blocked = TRUE, svg = TRUE),
    lowercase   = list(files = list("notes.md" = "see pmbb-0000000012345"), blocked = TRUE),
    embedded    = list(files = list("notes.md" = sprintf("sample_%s_A", fake_id)), blocked = TRUE),
    truncated   = list(files = list("notes.md" = "PMBB00001234"), blocked = TRUE),
    short       = list(files = list("notes.md" = "the PMBB12 cohort"), blocked = FALSE),
    png_genomic = list(files = list("report.html" = paste0('<img src="data:image/png;base64,', png_noise, '">', genomics)), blocked = FALSE),
    synthetic   = list(files = list("Synthetic/fixture.csv" = c("person_id,age", paste0(fake_id, ",50"))), blocked = TRUE)
  )
}

test_that("pre-commit hook blocks PMBB identifiers and masks its output", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_on_os("windows")
  skip_if(Sys.which("git") == "", "git is not installed")
  modes <- if (nzchar(Sys.which("rg"))) c(TRUE, FALSE) else FALSE
  for (with_rg in modes) {
    for (case_name in names(hook_cases())) {
      case <- hook_cases()[[case_name]]
      proj <- hook_project()
      result <- try_commit(proj, case$files, with_rg = with_rg)
      label <- paste(case_name, if (with_rg) "(rg)" else "(grep)")
      expect_identical(result$status != 0, case$blocked, label = label)
      expect_false(grepl("0000000012345", result$stderr, fixed = TRUE), label = label)
      if (isTRUE(case$svg)) {
        expect_true(grepl("embedded SVG", result$stderr, fixed = TRUE), label = label)
      }
    }
  }
})

test_that("pre-commit hook allows a clean 10 MB HTML report", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_on_os("windows")
  skip_if(Sys.which("git") == "", "git is not installed")
  proj <- hook_project()
  rows <- rep("<tr><td>chr2:123456789</td><td>0.05</td></tr>", 230000)
  result <- try_commit(proj, list("report.html" = rows))
  expect_true(file.size(file.path(proj, "report.html")) > 10e6)
  expect_equal(result$status, 0)
})

# Helpers for the run script tests: a fake curl records its arguments, so the
# notification code runs without network access.
run_pipeline <- function(targets_script, notify = "slack", curl_status = 0) {
  proj <- withr::local_tempdir(.local_envir = parent.frame())
  suppressMessages(populate_targets_proj("test", path = proj, overwrite = TRUE, git_safeguards = FALSE))
  writeLines(targets_script, file.path(proj, "_targets.R"))
  bin <- withr::local_tempdir(.local_envir = parent.frame())
  log <- file.path(bin, "curl.log")
  writeLines(c("#!/bin/sh", sprintf('printf "%%s\\n" "$@" >> "%s"', log), sprintf("exit %d", curl_status)),
             file.path(bin, "curl"))
  Sys.chmod(file.path(bin, "curl"), "755")
  env <- c("current",
           PATH = paste(bin, Sys.getenv("PATH"), sep = .Platform$path.sep),
           LEVINMISC_NOTIFY = notify,
           LEVINMISC_SLACK_WEBHOOK = "https://hooks.example.invalid/services/T0/B0/X0")
  result <- processx::run(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), ".run-pipeline.R", wd = proj,
                          env = env, error_on_status = FALSE)
  result$curl_log <- if (file.exists(log)) paste(readLines(log), collapse = "\n") else NULL
  result
}

passing_pipeline <- c("library(targets)", "list(tar_target(a, 1), tar_target(b, a + 1))")
failing_pipeline <- c("library(targets)",
                      "list(tar_target(a, 1), tar_target(b, stop('bad value PMBB0000000099999')))")

test_that(".run-pipeline.R reports a successful run", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_if_not_installed("targets")
  skip_on_os("windows")
  result <- run_pipeline(passing_pipeline)
  expect_equal(result$status, 0)
  expect_true(grepl("completed", result$curl_log, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_true(grepl("Completed: 2", result$curl_log, fixed = TRUE))
})

test_that(".run-pipeline.R reports a failure without error text or identifiers", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_if_not_installed("targets")
  skip_on_os("windows")
  result <- run_pipeline(failing_pipeline)
  expect_equal(result$status, 1)
  expect_true(grepl("FAILED", result$curl_log, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_true(grepl("Errored targets: b", result$curl_log, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_false(grepl("bad value", result$curl_log, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_false(grepl("0000000099999", result$curl_log, fixed = TRUE))
})

test_that(".run-pipeline.R keeps the pipeline status when the notification fails", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_if_not_installed("targets")
  skip_on_os("windows")
  result <- run_pipeline(passing_pipeline, curl_status = 7)
  expect_equal(result$status, 0)
  expect_true(grepl("Notification failed", result$stderr, fixed = TRUE))
})

test_that(".run-pipeline.R sends nothing when notifications are off", {
  skip_on_cran()
  skip_if_not_installed("targets")
  skip_on_os("windows")
  result <- run_pipeline(passing_pipeline, notify = "")
  expect_equal(result$status, 0)
  expect_null(result$curl_log)
})
```

### Use {crew} for parallelization

The `crew` and `crew.cluster` packages have enabled the use of heterogenous workers (<https://books.ropensci.org/targets/crew.html#heterogeneous-workers>), that can be used to deploy `targets` pipelines either locally or on HPC resources. The `use_crew_lsf()` function is designed to return a block of code to rapidly enable the use of heterogeneous workers on the Penn LPC. By default, this function creates workers that submit to different queues (eg. `voltron_normal`, `voltron_long`), and allocate different resources (eg. a "normal" worker will use 1 core and 16GB memory, while a "long" worker will use 1 core and 10GB memory).

`use_crew_lsf()` takes the same `runtime` argument as `populate_targets_proj()`, which controls the shell lines that open each worker script. Under `"container"` the worker exports `R_LIBS_USER` and `SINGULARITY_BIND` and then runs R through `singularity exec`; under `"native"` it runs `module load R/4.5` and nothing else, so the project library comes from `renv/activate.R` (`crew_options_lsf()` defaults `cwd` to the project directory). The two branches also differ in the `crew.cluster` interface they emit: the container branch keeps the older `lsf_*` arguments to `crew_controller_lsf()`, which is what the `crew.cluster` build inside the image understands, while the native branch uses the `crew_options_lsf()` interface that replaced them.
    
```{r function-use_crew_lsf}
#' Use crew lsf to execute a targets pipeline using the LSF HPC scheduler
#' 
#' @description
#' `r lifecycle::badge("experimental")`
#' 
#' This function returns a template for using `crew.cluster` in a targets project, enabling the parallel execution of a targets workflow. By default, the template is pre-filled using parameters specific to the LPC system at Penn. By default, this function creates workers that submit to different queues (eg. `voltron_normal`, `voltron_long`), and allocate different resources (eg. a "normal" worker will use 1 core and 16GB memory, while a "long" worker will use 1 core and 10GB memory).
#'
#' The `runtime` argument selects the R installation the workers run against. `"native"`, the default, loads the LPC's R module and leaves the package library to `renv`; `"container"` runs each worker inside the LPC's RStudio Singularity image instead. Use `"container"` only when the project library was built against that image: a worker that loads a library built for a different R version fails with errors such as `unused arguments (controller = ...)`, because the worker and the controller then run different `crew` versions.
#'
#' @param runtime (character) R runtime the LSF workers use: `"native"` (the default) for the module-provided R, or `"container"` for the LPC RStudio Singularity image
#' @param path (character) project directory the pipeline runs in, defaulting to the working directory. It supplies the controller names and, under the container runtime, the working directory each worker runs in
#'
#' @return A code block to copy/paste into a targets project
#'
#' @export
#' @concept targets

use_crew_lsf <- function(runtime = c("native", "container"), path = ".") {
  runtime <- rlang::arg_match(runtime)

  # The controller names and the container's working directory both come from
  # the project directory, taken as an argument rather than searched for: a
  # rprojroot-style search walks up from the working directory and lands in a
  # parent when the project carries no .Rproj, DESCRIPTION or .git marker.
  path <- fs::path_norm(fs::path_abs(path))
  title <- basename(path)

  # The "container" runtime executes each worker inside the LPC's RStudio
  # image, so `R_LIBS_USER` has to name a library built against that image's R.
  # The "native" runtime loads the LPC's R module instead and leaves the library
  # to `renv/activate.R`, because `crew_options_lsf()` defaults `cwd` to the
  # directory the controllers were built in - the project directory.
  container_image <- "/project/voltron/rstudio/containers/bioconductor-tidyverse_3.17.sif"
  container_library <- "$HOME/R/rocker-rstudio/bioconductor-tidyverse_3.17"
  container_bind <- "/project/:/project/, /appl/:/appl/, /lsf/:/lsf/, /scratch/:/scratch, /static:/static"
  r_module <- lpc_r_module

  # Shell lines that open each worker script, rendered as the elements of a
  # `script_lines = c(...)` call. crew appends its own `Rscript -e '...'` after
  # them, so under the container runtime the `singularity exec` line comes last
  # and ends in a line continuation.
  worker_lines <- function(queue, threads, indent) {
    lines <- c(
      paste0("#BSUB-q ", queue),
      if (runtime == "container") {
        paste0("export R_LIBS_USER=", container_library)
      } else {
        paste0("module load ", r_module)
      },
      "export TMPDIR=/scratch",
      paste0("export OMP_NUM_THREADS=", threads),
      if (runtime == "container") {
        c(
          paste0("export SINGULARITY_BIND='", container_bind, "'"),
          paste0("singularity exec --pwd ", path, " ", container_image, " \\")
        )
      }
    )

    paste0(strrep(" ", indent), encodeString(lines, quote = "\""), collapse = ",\n")
  }

  # A single `crew_controller_lsf()` call, rendered as the source the user
  # pastes into their pipeline. The native runtime uses the current
  # `crew_options_lsf()` interface; the container runtime keeps the `lsf_*`
  # arguments it replaced, which are what the crew.cluster build inside the
  # image understands.
  controller <- function(suffix, workers, queue, memory, threads = 1, cores = NULL) {
    if (runtime == "container") {
      glue::glue(
        "controller_lsf_{suffix} <- crew.cluster::crew_controller_lsf(
  name = '{title}_{suffix}',
  workers = {workers}L,{cores_line}
  lsf_memory_gigabytes_limit = {memory},
  script_dir = tools::R_user_dir('crew.cluster', which = 'cache'),
  lsf_log_output = 'build_logs/crew-%J.log',
  lsf_log_error = 'build_logs/crew-%J.err',
  script_lines = c(
{worker_lines(queue, threads, indent = 4)}
  ),
  verbose = TRUE
)",
        cores_line = if (is.null(cores)) "" else paste0("\n  lsf_cores = ", cores, ",")
      )
    } else {
      glue::glue(
        "controller_lsf_{suffix} <- crew.cluster::crew_controller_lsf(
  name = '{title}_{suffix}',
  workers = {workers}L,
  options_cluster = crew.cluster::crew_options_lsf(
    verbose = TRUE,
    script_directory = tools::R_user_dir('crew.cluster', which = 'cache'),
    script_lines = c(
{worker_lines(queue, threads, indent = 6)}
    ),
    log_output = 'build_logs/crew-%J.log',
    log_error = 'build_logs/crew-%J.err',
    memory_gigabytes_limit = {memory}{cores_line}
  )
)",
        cores_line = if (is.null(cores)) "" else paste0(",\n    cores = ", cores)
      )
    }
  }

  command <- glue::glue(
    "library(targets)
library(tarchetypes)
library(crew)
library(crew.cluster)

controller_local <- crew_controller_local(
  name = '{title}_local',
  workers = 1,
  seconds_idle = 10
)

{controller('normal', 20, 'voltron_normal', 16)}

{controller('long', 150, 'voltron_long', 10)}

{controller('highmem', 5, 'voltron_normal', 96)}

{controller('multicore', 5, 'voltron_normal', 96, threads = 16, cores = 16)}

# define some global options/functions common to all targets
options(tidyverse.quiet = TRUE)

tar_option_set(
  packages = c('tidyverse', 'targets', 'tarchetypes', 'arrow', 'vroom', 'data.table', 'gt', 'crew', 'crew.cluster'),
  controller = crew::crew_controller_group(controller_lsf_long, controller_lsf_normal, controller_lsf_highmem, controller_lsf_multicore, controller_local),
  resources = tar_resources(
    crew = tar_resources_crew(controller = '{title}_normal')
  ),
  storage = 'worker',
  retrieval = 'worker',
  cue = tar_cue(format = FALSE)
)"
  )

  cli::cli_h1("Copy the below code to the `global` chunk in your targets project:")

  return(command)
}
```

  
```{r example-use_crew_lsf, eval=FALSE}

use_crew_lsf()
use_crew_lsf(runtime = "container")
#' }
```
  
```{r tests-use_crew_lsf}
test_that("use_crew_lsf works", {
  expect_true(inherits(use_crew_lsf, "function"))
})

test_that("use_crew_lsf defaults to the native runtime", {
  template <- suppressMessages(use_crew_lsf())
  expect_identical(
    as.character(template),
    as.character(suppressMessages(use_crew_lsf(runtime = "native")))
  )
  expect_true(grepl("module load R/", template, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_false(grepl("singularity exec", template, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_false(grepl("R_LIBS_USER", template, fixed = TRUE))
})

test_that("use_crew_lsf runs workers in the image under the container runtime", {
  template <- suppressMessages(use_crew_lsf(runtime = "container"))
  expect_true(grepl("singularity exec", template, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_true(grepl("export SINGULARITY_BIND=", template, fixed = TRUE))
  expect_false(grepl("module load", template, fixed = TRUE))
})

test_that("use_crew_lsf returns parseable R code for either runtime", {
  for (runtime in c("container", "native")) {
    template <- suppressMessages(use_crew_lsf(runtime = runtime))
    expect_true(length(parse(text = template)) > 0)
  }
})

test_that("use_crew_lsf rejects an unknown runtime", {
  expect_error(use_crew_lsf(runtime = "singularity"), "must be one of")
})
```
